prompt_text: What is the best service to check if AI engines like ChatGPT recommend my small business?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: There’s no single “AI checker” — you get the best result by (A) owning and optimizing your core business listings (Google Business Profile, Bing Places, Apple Maps, Yelp, etc.), (B) using a local-listings/audit service (Yext, BrightLocal, Moz Local) to verify distribution and accuracy, and (C) directly testing LLMs (ChatGPT, Bard, Bing Chat, Claude) with location-aware prompts. Yext or BrightLocal are the most useful single services for auditing/updating what feeds into search/AI.

What to do, step‑by‑step
1. Claim and optimize core listings
   - Google Business Profile (essential), Bing Places, Apple Business Connect, Yelp, Facebook, TripAdvisor (if relevant).
   - Ensure NAP (name, address, phone), hours, categories and high-quality photos are correct.

2. Publish structured data on your website
   - Add LocalBusiness/Organization schema (JSON‑LD).
   - Test with Google’s Rich Results Test and the Schema Markup Validator.

3. Run a listings/knowledge audit (recommended services)
   - Yext: centralized control/distribution to many platforms; helps feed knowledge graphs and has AI integrations.
   - BrightLocal: thorough local SEO audits, citation tracking, rank checks and reviews monitoring.
   - Moz Local or Synup: alternatives for citation management and distribution.
   These services scan directory coverage, duplicates, and inaccuracies — fixing them improves the chance AI systems will surface your business.

4. Check Knowledge Graph / API presence
   - Use Google’s Knowledge Graph Search API and Google Maps (Place ID) to see if you have a knowledge panel.
   - If you have a Google Knowledge Panel, claim it.

5. Directly test AI engines
   - ChatGPT: use a model with browsing enabled or the web plugin (plain ChatGPT without web access may be out-of-date). Prompt examples:
     - “Recommend a [service] near [your city or ZIP]. List top 5 businesses and why.” 
     - “Is [Your Business Name] in [City]? Would you recommend them for [service]?”
   - Google Bard, Bing Chat, Anthropic Claude: ask similar prompts. Include your city/ZIP and common user intent phrases (“best”, “near me”, “affordable”, etc.).
   - Try multiple phrasings and test from different IP/locations if possible (LLMs sometimes use location cues).

6. Monitor reviews & ratings
   - Many AI assistants weigh ratings and review volume. Keep collecting and responding to reviews.

Why Yext / BrightLocal?
- Yext: strong for centralized knowledge management and distribution to platforms and some AI consumers; good if you want one place to push factual data to many endpoints.
- BrightLocal: excellent for diagnostics — shows where you appear, ranking in local packs, citation issues, and gives actionable local SEO recommendations.

What to expect from LLMs
- LLMs don’t always cite or surface the same sources search engines do; answers can vary by model, prompt, and whether the model has live web access. Even if you’re listed everywhere, an LLM might not “recommend” you unless signals (ratings, citations, website content, knowledge panel) are strong.

If you want, tell me:
- your business name + city/ZIP and whether you’ve claimed Google Business Profile, and I’ll suggest the highest‑impact next steps (and sample prompts to test ChatGPT/Bard).
session_note: run_channel caveat: API results can differ from logged-in consumer apps, no memory, no personalization.
